explanation: Fires on the word right after an interrogative 'what/which' (+ kind/sort/type/portion/revision/one), most strongly on ' of' in 'what kind of', 'what sort of', 'what portion of', 'which one of'; moderately on the noun/adjective directly following 'what' ('what other', 'what new', 'what extent', 'how high'). Near zero elsewhere.

Mixture: symbol-heavy tokens in code/regex ('(.', '([^', '[*]', '."\'), the '+/-' in 'mean +/- SD' statistics, mid-identifier camelCase pieces like 'numberOf'/'arrayOf'/'getCurrent', plus some ordinary words ('southeastern', 'health-care'). No single shared feature.

Fires on a non-initial piece of a multi-token name: CamelCase class/type names and package path parts in code (UIImagePickerController, TextInputType, android.content.Intent, stdbool, HostException), and continuation fragments of proper names or rare words in prose (B-ingham-ton, Phil-ippi, pilgr-ims, McCorm-ack, babys-itters).
No clear pattern: top tokens range across verbs ('trying', 'transform', 'locate'), nouns ('post', 'body', 'articles'), pronouns ('you', 'I'), digits in dates/URLs and code variables. Hard to predict.

Fires on the first subword piece of a capitalized word that the tokenizer splits, e.g. ' Ind' (Indus, Individually, Indictable), ' Sh' (Shaukat, Shandong, Shaving), ' Th' (Thematic), ' St', ' Sp', ' All'(ergy), often at sentence start or in proper nouns. Whole-word capitalized tokens and lowercase fragments give little.

Two unrelated jobs: (1) a person's first name in a sequence of named people or after a title ('Karl' Liebknecht, 'Ben' Jonson, 'Robert', 'Sam', 'James', 'Barack'); (2) the 'haem/hem' fragment of haemorrhage/hemophilia/hemodialysis and similar biomedical word-start fragments (ter-atogenesis, alo-pecia).

Mixed: restrictive/hedging adverbs ('strictly', 'purely', 'vaguely'), the prefix 'non' in 'noncancerous/non-radial', and inner pieces of technical compounds ('per-maf-rost', 'cy-topl-asm', 'body mass', 'spinal cord', 'carbox-y'), plus misc code tokens. No single rule.

Fires on a determiner/article ('a', 'an', 'the') directly after a copula or partitive that introduces a definition or description: 'X is a ...', 'It's a ...', 'One of the ...', 'Many of the ...', 'such a'. Articles in other positions are weak.

Fires on words about timekeeping and precise measurement/orientation: clocks, crystal oscillators, time synchronization, watches, pendulum, timezone, Date/epoch, plus balance/sensing terms (vestibular, spirit level, suprachiasmatic, localization, interferometer). Strongest on the head term of a timing device.

Fires inside software license boilerplate: strongest on ' or' in 'version 3 of the License, or (at your option)', and on ' file'/'.txt' after 'LICENSE' ('see the LICENSE file'), also 'writing' in 'agreed to in writing'. Outside license headers it is weak.

Fires on 'See' starting a reference instruction in license/copyright headers ('See the License for...', 'See LICENSE.txt', 'see the file COPYING'), and more weakly on similar referral verbs ('Please refer to', 'check out', 'Click', 'read our guide').

Mixture around promotional descriptions of places/organizations: possessive "'s" after a city/company ('Denver's top hotels', "India's largest"), articles in 'one of the'/'is truly a', and the verb 'turn' ('turn to a professional', 'turn right'). Not one coherent cue.

Fires on a head noun that names a collective or sampled set after a modifier noun: 'blood samples', 'bird species', 'crew members', 'staff member', 'meat products'; also on 'exist/exists' in 'there exist(s)'. Strongest on 'samples', 'species', 'member(s)'.

Fires on the token right after a (usually plural or compound) noun subject, especially a verb with number disagreement ('The patients is', 'my local images is', 'checkboxes has', 'Dataclasses is'), and on a second noun stacked onto a plural noun ('cadherins receptors', 'robots information').

Fires on the preposition or verb linking a patient/subject to a clinical setting or diagnostic means: 'presented to', 'admitted to', 'referred to', 'transported to', 'detected by', 'lesion on angiography', 'while receiving', 'already on warfarin'. Strongest in medical case reports.

Fires on pieces of chemistry and scientific nomenclature: bond notation ('C=C'), element symbols and formula parts (Zn, Te, C4), chemical fragments ('-rich', 'yl', 'methyl', 'ethyl'), and some other technical words ('dashed', 'ground', 'tin oxide'). Ordinary prose gives nothing.

Mixture: ' here' in 'click here', word-final pieces of names and rare words ('ILL'inois, 'rd', 'ung', 'ized'), and the end of fixed phrases ('no more', "don't mean", 'changed my mind', 'not wanted'). No common cue.

Fires on ' to' that introduces a purpose clause after 'used'/'use X'/'uses Y' ('was used to estimate', 'use that to work with', 'uses the printer driver to convert'); also Turkish 'ile'/Hungarian instrumental suffixes. Other uses of 'to' are weak.

Fires on early tokens of a StackOverflow-style question (title and first sentence after 'Q:'): 'I am', 'Here is my', 'not' in 'X not working', 'works fine but', 'Say I have'. Weak once the question body moves into code or detail.
No clear pattern: tokens include 'by' in 'generated by', 'Press' in 'University Press', 'bedrooms', 'assumed', code identifiers, digits and adverbs. Not predictable from these examples.

Mixed: the comma after a name or descriptor in biographical/appositive phrases ('engineer and entrepreneur,', 'Born in Suzhou,'), and emphasis/negation words in a verb phrase ('to really', 'actually', 'may not', "can't"). Two loosely related or unrelated cues.
